episodes.189273: An unstable atmosphere and a strong upper level disturbance resulted in strong thunderstorms.
episodes.189423: A frontal system came through central California on night from April 12 into April 13, bringing widespread rain and gusty winds. The post-frontal environment was conducive for convective activity.
episodes.189432: A cold front brought widespread soaking rainfall to the area. This rainfall combined with significant snowpack loss and saturated grounds to produce minor to moderate river flooding, with isolated flash flooding across the mountains. Repeated rounds of rain compressed, warmed, and ripened the area snowpack in advance of the heavier rain on Friday the 12th.  The combination of rain, strong winds, and high dew points in excess of  50F over the ripe snow led to rapid melt with up to 4��� water loss. Complete melt-out occurred below 2,000 ft. The ground was bare south of the foothills; however soils were saturated and offered little storage for runoff. Rainfall ranged from 1 to 2 inches for most of the region, with amounts of 2 to 3 inches in the mountains.
episodes.189623: A potent system moved through the southern half of NC during the afternoon and evening hours, with thunderstorms becoming severe as they moved through the southern Piedmont of NC, and into the southern coastal plain counties, all the way to the coast through mid evening. Most of the severe reports were from thunderstorm winds, but isolated severe hail fell as well.
episodes.189709: Showers and thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of April 11th due to the combination of unseasonably warm temperatures and a passing disturbance. Storms crossed in from the Ohio River Valley during the early afternoon and continued an eastward progression into the evening. A swath of tree damage and power outages were observed from Mingo County to the eastern half of the West Virginia from damaging wind gusts. Storms pressed eastward late on the evening of April 11th.||In addition, numerous areas of flooding transpired that afternoon and evening in response to heavy downpours and training storms throughout the state. The Charleston airport set records for the wettest April as a result of observing 3.32 inches of rainfall on April 11th, breaking the old record of 1.83 inches set back in 1965.||High water issues along state roads were the main impacts from the flooding, some of which needed water rescues for cars that drove into these trouble spots. Excess water eventually drained into the Ohio River on the 12th and 13th of April, returning to its banks a few days later. One fatality occurred in Wood County on the 14th, when a motorist drove past high water signs and their vehicle became submerged.
episodes.189742: A combination of 1 to 2 inches of rain...along with snow melt...led to minor flooding along the Piscataquis River in Dover-Foxcroft. The river crested slightly over a half foot above flood stage during the early morning hours of the 13th. The river fell back below flood stage that afternoon. The flooding was minor...mostly affecting low land areas along the river. Minor flooding was also reported on Back Road in Abbot...along with some recreational fields in Guilford.
episodes.190071: An advancing low pressure system entered into the Ohio Valley on April 11th and set forth strong thunderstorms and heavy downpours. Storms tracked through initially early in the afternoon, stirring up strong winds that blew down a tree near the town of Ironton. As multiple rounds of showers and storms pressed across Ohio, heavy downpours over already saturated soils drained into the local creeks and streams and resulted in river flooding beginning that evening. Flooding eventually stemmed into the Ohio River on the 13th as water flowed down from New York and Pennsylvania, where heavy rain also occurred. Several gauges along the Ohio River from Willow Island Lock, Marietta, and Pomeroy rose above flood stage, resulting in flooded streets in the nearby towns. The river returned below flood at all three locations on April 14th and 15th.
episodes.190330: Mid-level instability lead to cu-buildups and some more organized thunderstorms across Humboldt and Lander. These storms produce gusty outflow winds.
episodes.190563: A potent system brought scattered strong to severe thunderstorms to the waters south of the Croatan and Roanoke Sounds and across the coastal waters south of Oregon Inlet on the evening of April 12th. Thunderstorms started out across the Piedmont of North Carolina and quickly raced eastward as a line before entering the offshore waters of Eastern North Carolina Friday evening bringing damaging wind gusts with them.
episodes.191085: Breezy easterlies steered scattered showers over eastern Puerto Rico, promoting a rise in Rio Blanco.

A combination of rain and snow melt led to minor flooding along portions of the Piscataquis River. The flooding impacted mostly low land areas along the river.

Heavy rain and snowmelt caused the Kennebec River to swell and flood portion of downtown Augusta. The USGS river gage exceeded the 12 foot flood stage a little after 1 am on the 13th and remained above flood stage through late morning on the 15th, cresting at 16.7 feet on the 13th. This resulted in flooding of Mill Park and basements of buildings along Water Street.

The Ohio River at Willow Island Lock exceeded its flood stage during the pre-dawn hours on the 13th of April. The river continued to rise to a crest of around 38.8 feet early on the 14th, then fell below flood stage later that night. Ohio State 7, Township Road 443, and Township Road 19 at Newell Run and Lenards Landing flooded while the river spilled out of its banks.

The Ohio River at Point Pleasant rose above flood stage early in the morning of April 13th.  After reaching a crest of around 43.8 feet early on the 15th, the river descended below flood stage the morning of April 16th. While the river was out of its banks, water spilled onto Route 21 at Eight Mile Creek above Ambrosia. Flooding also impacted Routes 30 and 62 near Rockcastle Creek and Ambrosia, Ohio Route 7 at Kyger Creek and Addison, Little Kyger Road and Blaville Road in Ohio, and low lying areas surrounding Point Pleasant.

The Ohio River at Racine Lock rose above its flood stage of 41 feet early in the morning of April 13th. After reaching a crest of around 44.6 feet on the afternoon of the 14th, the river returned below flood stage the next evening. West Virginia Route 62 flooded just below Racine Lock at West Creek due to the river spilling out of its banks. Sections of Ohio Route 124 and areas of Ravenswood also flooded.

Heavy rain and snowmelt caused the Androscoggin River to rise above flood stage between Bethel and Jay. The USGS river gage in Rumford rose above flood stage of 15.0 feet on the morning of the 15th, cresting just a few inches higher later that day. The impacts include flooding along North Road north of Gibson Road in Bethel and along Intervale Road in Hanover. Route 140 was closed between Dixfield and Jay.

Heavy rain and snowmelt caused the Kennebec River to swell and flood parts of downtown Hallowell. The USGS river gage exceeded the 11 foot flood stage a little after 5 am on the 13th and remained above flood stage through late morning on the 14th, cresting at 13.7 feet in moderate flood stage. Water was up to the basements of business off of Front Street. Pre-emptive sandbagging prevented property damage.
One to three feet of flooding was reported on the onramp from MacArthur to Eastbound Interstate 580.
Around 1 foot of water was reported on westbound California Highway 237 just east of Zanker.

Heavy rain and snowmelt resulted in minor flooding across the Upper Kennebec River watershed. In Skowhegan, high flows estimated around 60 kcfs at the Weston Dam resulted in flooding along East River Road. The high flows peaked late on the 13th and gradually receded by the 15th.
The right turn lane from Ferguson Road to California Route 152 was flooded.
Heavy rain and snowmelt caused rises on the Kennebec River. In Clinton, River Road flooded near Peavy Road on the evening of the 13th. The floodwaters receded on the morning of the 14th.
